actions.action: Check soil moisture 3-4 inches down beside the root ball
If dry, water slowly and deeply at the base
If soggy, hold off watering and fix drainage
Flush fertilizer granules with a long, slow soak
Apply 2-3 inches of mulch over the root zone, kept back from the stems
Scratch-test stems to check whether they are alive
After new growth is established, prune stems that stay dead
Install temporary afternoon shade such as shade cloth
If the soil is heavy clay, replant slightly high or amend the bed with pine bark

reason: The answer headlines transplant stress and lists heat/drought as only one of several causes, and the fix (frequent deep watering plus shade) appears only as conditional, check-first watering and an optional shade suggestion; nothing in it is likely to cause harm.
